explanations: There is no defect. Every test starts from a truncated schema in beforeEach, so no test depends on rows left by another. Every async assertion is awaited (including `await expect(...).rejects`), so failures cannot be silently skipped. The concurrent dedupe test is valid against a real database: the unique constraint on dedupe_key plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING means the second insert waits for the first transaction and then returns 0 rows, and its follow-up SELECT runs after the first commit, so both calls return the same id. The pool is closed in afterAll, so the runner does not hang.

Postgres blocks a conflicting insert on a unique index until the other transaction finishes; after the first commits, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING yields rowCount 0 and the SELECT finds the committed row. Promise.all starts both calls concurrently, not sequentially. There is no in-process lock in NotificationService. TRUNCATE runs only in beforeEach, once per test.

An integration test should verify observable side effects in the database; the assertion confirms the ROLLBACK path leaves no partial state. In the code the preference check comes before any insert, so the outbox is not written first. Vitest has no minimum assertion count. TRUNCATE is not what this assertion is about; it filters on rows that would have been created by this call.

A pg Pool keeps idle client sockets open until they time out or pool.end() is called, which keeps the Node process alive after tests finish. Isolation between tests comes from TRUNCATE in beforeEach, not from closing the pool, so neither constraint violations nor leaked rows follow. Closing the pool has nothing to do with locks taken by TRUNCATE.
